<div id="bx-article">

  <div class="bx-pills">
    <span class="bx-pill">Development</span>
    <span class="bx-pill">PHP</span>
    <span class="bx-pill">Cron</span>
    <span class="bx-pill">Automation</span>
  </div>

  <p class="bx-lede">A cron job that runs fine in testing can still fail silently in production for months before anyone notices. PHP cron jobs need a few extra habits beyond a working script and a crontab line to actually run reliably.</p>

  <div class="bx-section-head">
    <span class="bx-num">01</span>
    <h2 class="bx-h2" id="why-php-cron-jobs-still-break-in-production">Why PHP Cron Jobs Still Break in Production</h2>
    <div class="bx-rule"></div>
  </div>

  <p>Cron runs a script with almost none of the environment a terminal session normally provides. No shell profile, no PATH beyond a minimal default, no working directory guarantee.</p>

  <p>A script that works perfectly when run by hand can fail the moment cron runs it, often for reasons that never show up anywhere because nothing was watching for them.</p>

  <div class="bx-ad">
    <script async src="https://pagead2.googlesyndication.com/pagead/js/adsbygoogle.js?client=ca-pub-3931314195561246" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
    <ins class="adsbygoogle" style="display:block" data-ad-client="ca-pub-3931314195561246" data-ad-slot="4249015278" data-ad-format="auto" data-full-width-responsive="true"></ins>
    <script>(adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});</script>
  </div>

  <div class="bx-section-head">
    <span class="bx-num">02</span>
    <h2 class="bx-h2" id="writing-a-crontab-entry-that-actually-works">Writing a Crontab Entry That Actually Works</h2>
    <div class="bx-rule"></div>
  </div>

  <p>Every path in a crontab entry should be absolute. Cron has no idea where a project lives unless it is told explicitly, every single time.</p>

  <div class="bx-code-wrap">
    <div class="bx-code-title">crontab -e</div>
    <pre><code><span class="tok-cm"># run every 15 minutes, full paths, output redirected to a real log file</span>
*/15 * * * * /usr/bin/php /var/www/app/tasks/sync_inventory.php >> /var/log/app/cron.log 2>&1</code></pre>
  </div>

  <p>Redirecting both standard output and standard error into a log file turns a silent failure into something that can actually be found and investigated later.</p>

  <p>The <a href="https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/crontab.5.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">crontab(5) man page</a> documents every field in that schedule expression in detail, worth bookmarking for any future PHP cron jobs that need a less common interval than every 15 minutes. Libraries like <a href="https://github.com/peppeocchi/php-cron-scheduler" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><code>php-cron-scheduler</code></a> wrap this same idea into a fluent API for projects that want schedules defined directly in PHP instead of raw crontab syntax.</p>

  <div class="bx-section-head">
    <span class="bx-num">03</span>
    <h2 class="bx-h2" id="preventing-overlapping-runs-with-a-file-lock">Preventing Overlapping Runs With a File Lock</h2>
    <div class="bx-rule"></div>
  </div>

  <p>A task scheduled every minute that occasionally takes two minutes will eventually have two copies of itself running at once, each one working against the same data.</p>

  <div class="bx-code-wrap">
    <div class="bx-code-title">locked_task.php</div>
    <pre><code><span class="tok-val">$lockFile</span> = __DIR__ . <span class="tok-str">'/task.lock'</span>;
<span class="tok-val">$handle</span> = fopen(<span class="tok-val">$lockFile</span>, <span class="tok-str">'c'</span>);

<span class="tok-kw">if</span> (!flock(<span class="tok-val">$handle</span>, LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)) {
    fwrite(STDERR, <span class="tok-str">"Another instance is still running. Exiting.\n"</span>);
    <span class="tok-kw">exit</span>(<span class="tok-val">1</span>);
}

<span class="tok-fn">echo</span> <span class="tok-str">"Lock acquired, running task...\n"</span>;
sleep(<span class="tok-val">2</span>);
<span class="tok-fn">echo</span> <span class="tok-str">"Task finished, releasing lock.\n"</span>;

flock(<span class="tok-val">$handle</span>, LOCK_UN);
fclose(<span class="tok-val">$handle</span>);</code></pre>
  </div>

  <p>Starting the same script twice, a fraction of a second apart, shows exactly what should happen: one run finishes normally, the other exits immediately instead of colliding with it.</p>

  <div class="bx-shot">
    <img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Real terminal output showing two php processes started 0.3 seconds apart, the first acquiring the lock and finishing normally while the second exits immediately because the lock is already held" />
  </div>
  <p class="bx-shot-caption">Actual output from starting locked_task.php twice, 0.3 seconds apart.</p>

  <p>This works well on a single server. For PHP cron jobs that might run on more than one server behind a load balancer, the same Redis backed locking approach covered in <a href="/php-rate-limiting/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">PHP rate limiting</a> replaces the local file lock with a shared one every server can see.</p>

  <p>PHP's own <a href="https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.flock.php" target="_blank" rel="noopener">flock() manual page</a> documents the LOCK_EX and LOCK_NB flags used above in full detail, including how behavior differs across filesystem types.</p>

  <div class="bx-section-head">
    <span class="bx-num">04</span>
    <h2 class="bx-h2" id="logging-every-run-so-failures-are-visible">Logging Every Run So Failures Are Visible</h2>
    <div class="bx-rule"></div>
  </div>

  <p>A cron job has no terminal in front of it. Whatever is not written to a log did not happen as far as anyone monitoring the system is concerned.</p>

  <div class="bx-code-wrap">
    <div class="bx-code-title">logged_task.php</div>
    <pre><code><span class="tok-kw">function</span> <span class="tok-fn">log_line</span>(<span class="tok-kw">string</span> <span class="tok-val">$level</span>, <span class="tok-kw">string</span> <span class="tok-val">$message</span>): <span class="tok-kw">void</span> {
    <span class="tok-val">$line</span> = sprintf(<span class="tok-str">"[%s] %s: %s\n"</span>, date(<span class="tok-str">'Y-m-d H:i:s'</span>), <span class="tok-val">$level</span>, <span class="tok-val">$message</span>);
    file_put_contents(__DIR__ . <span class="tok-str">'/task.log'</span>, <span class="tok-val">$line</span>, FILE_APPEND);
}

<span class="tok-fn">log_line</span>(<span class="tok-str">'INFO'</span>, <span class="tok-str">'sync_inventory started'</span>);

<span class="tok-kw">try</span> {
    <span class="tok-kw">if</span> (!file_exists(<span class="tok-str">'/tmp/feed.csv'</span>)) {
        <span class="tok-kw">throw new</span> RuntimeException(<span class="tok-str">'feed file not found at /tmp/feed.csv'</span>);
    }
} <span class="tok-kw">catch</span> (RuntimeException <span class="tok-val">$e</span>) {
    <span class="tok-fn">log_line</span>(<span class="tok-str">'ERROR'</span>, <span class="tok-val">$e</span>->getMessage());
    <span class="tok-kw">exit</span>(<span class="tok-val">1</span>);
}

<span class="tok-fn">log_line</span>(<span class="tok-str">'INFO'</span>, <span class="tok-str">'sync_inventory finished successfully'</span>);</code></pre>
  </div>

  <p>Running this once against a missing feed file, then again after the file shows up, produces a log that tells the entire story without anyone needing to have been watching live.</p>

  <div class="bx-shot">
    <img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Real task.log output showing a timestamped ERROR line for a missing feed file, followed by a timestamped INFO line showing the next run started and finished successfully" />
  </div>
  <p class="bx-shot-caption">Actual task.log contents after one failed run and one successful run of the same script.</p>

  <p>Tools like <a href="https://crontab.guru/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">crontab.guru</a> make it easy to double check a schedule expression before trusting it, which matters just as much as the code running inside the task itself.</p>

  <p>A cron job that reads an external feed file should never trust its contents blindly either. The same validation habits covered in <a href="/validating-and-sanitizing-user-input-in-php-forms/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">validating and sanitizing user input in PHP forms</a> apply just as much here, since a cron job has no user in front of it to notice a bad value before it reaches the database.</p>

  <div class="bx-ad">
    <script async src="https://pagead2.googlesyndication.com/pagead/js/adsbygoogle.js?client=ca-pub-3931314195561246" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
    <ins class="adsbygoogle" style="display:block" data-ad-client="ca-pub-3931314195561246" data-ad-slot="4249015278" data-ad-format="auto" data-full-width-responsive="true"></ins>
    <script>(adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});</script>
  </div>

  <div class="bx-section-head">
    <span class="bx-num">05</span>
    <h2 class="bx-h2" id="catching-and-reporting-failures-automatically">Catching and Reporting Failures Automatically</h2>
    <div class="bx-rule"></div>
  </div>

  <p>A log file only helps if someone actually reads it. A failed run should also push a notification somewhere a person will actually see it.</p>

  <div class="bx-code-wrap">
    <div class="bx-code-title">alert_on_failure.php</div>
    <pre><code><span class="tok-kw">function</span> <span class="tok-fn">alert_failure</span>(<span class="tok-kw">string</span> <span class="tok-val">$task</span>, <span class="tok-kw">string</span> <span class="tok-val">$reason</span>): <span class="tok-kw">void</span> {
    <span class="tok-val">$payload</span> = json_encode([<span class="tok-str">'task'</span> => <span class="tok-val">$task</span>, <span class="tok-str">'reason'</span> => <span class="tok-val">$reason</span>]);

    <span class="tok-val">$ch</span> = curl_init(<span class="tok-str">'https://hooks.example.com/cron-alerts'</span>);
    curl_setopt(<span class="tok-val">$ch</span>, CURLOPT_POST, <span class="tok-val">true</span>);
    curl_setopt(<span class="tok-val">$ch</span>, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS, <span class="tok-val">$payload</span>);
    curl_setopt(<span class="tok-val">$ch</span>, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, [<span class="tok-str">'Content-Type: application/json'</span>]);
    curl_setopt(<span class="tok-val">$ch</span>, CURLOPT_TIMEOUT, <span class="tok-val">5</span>);
    curl_exec(<span class="tok-val">$ch</span>);
    curl_close(<span class="tok-val">$ch</span>);
}</code></pre>
  </div>

  <p>Building the receiving side of that webhook follows the same JSON request handling and clear error responses covered in <a href="/rest-api-in-php-without-a-framework/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">building a REST API in PHP without a framework</a>, just consuming a payload instead of serving one. PHP's <a href="https://curl.se/libcurl/c/curl_easy_setopt.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">libcurl option reference</a> documents every CURLOPT flag used above.</p>

  <p>A production setup would typically integrate with a service like <a href="https://sentry.io/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Sentry</a> instead of a custom webhook, since it handles retries, deduplication, and on call routing automatically for PHP cron jobs and every other part of an application.</p>

  <div class="bx-table-wrap">
    <table class="bx-table">
      <thead><tr><th>Approach</th><th>Good For</th><th>Tradeoff</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>Cron</td><td>Simple, time based, works everywhere</td><td>No built in overlap protection or retries</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Systemd timer</td><td>Better logging and dependency control</td><td>Only available on systemd based Linux hosts</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Queue worker</td><td>Event driven, retries, backpressure handling</td><td>More infrastructure to run and monitor</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>

  <p>The official <a href="https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.timer.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">systemd.timer documentation</a> covers the OnCalendar syntax and dependency options systemd timers offer beyond plain cron.</p>

  <div class="bx-section-head">
    <span class="bx-num">06</span>
    <h2 class="bx-h2" id="reusing-expensive-lookups-across-a-long-running-task">Reusing Expensive Lookups Across a Long Running Task</h2>
    <div class="bx-rule"></div>
  </div>

  <p>A cron job that queries the same reference data repeatedly during one run wastes cycles the same way a web request would. The <a href="/caching-database-queries-in-php-with-redis/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">caching database queries in PHP with Redis</a> pattern covered elsewhere in this series applies just as well inside a long running scheduled task.</p>

  <p>A job that downloads a file before processing it should also verify what that file actually is before trusting it, the same way covered in <a href="/php-file-upload-security/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">PHP file upload security</a>, since a scheduled download is no more trustworthy than a form upload.</p>

  <p>Symfony's <a href="https://symfony.com/doc/current/messenger.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Messenger component</a> is a common starting point in PHP if a queue worker turns out to be a better fit than PHP cron jobs for a particular piece of work.</p>

  <ul class="bx-checklist">
    <li><b>Use absolute paths everywhere:</b> reliable PHP cron jobs assume none of the shell environment a terminal session normally provides.</li>
    <li><b>Lock every task against overlapping runs:</b> a slow run and the next scheduled run should never execute together.</li>
    <li><b>Log start, success, and failure explicitly:</b> a job with no output leaves no trail when something goes wrong.</li>
    <li><b>Alert on failure, do not rely on someone reading logs:</b> a silent failure can run unnoticed for months.</li>
    <li><b>Redirect both stdout and stderr:</b> cron emails output by default in a way that is easy to miss entirely.</li>
  </ul>

  <div class="bx-section-head">
    <span class="bx-num">07</span>
    <h2 class="bx-h2" id="testing-a-scheduled-task-without-waiting-for-the-clock">Testing a Scheduled Task Without Waiting for the Clock</h2>
    <div class="bx-rule"></div>
  </div>

  <p>The exact command from the crontab line should be run by hand first, using the same absolute paths cron will use, not a shortcut version that only exists in a local shell.</p>

  <div class="bx-code-wrap">
    <div class="bx-code-title">terminal</div>
    <pre><code><span class="tok-cm"># run the exact command cron will run, before ever scheduling it</span>
/usr/bin/php /var/www/app/tasks/sync_inventory.php
echo <span class="tok-str">"exit code: $?"</span></code></pre>
  </div>

  <p>A task that only gets tested by waiting for the schedule to trigger it can take weeks to catch a bug that a single manual run would have caught immediately.</p>

  <svg width="100%" height="220" viewBox="0 0 800 220" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Diagram of cron triggering a task that acquires a lock, runs, logs its result, and alerts on failure" style="margin:26px 0;">

    <g font-family="Open Sans, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#2b2b2b">

      <text x="65" y="117" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">Cron Fires</text>

      <rect x="155" y="85" width="120" height="55" rx="8" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#5DB92E" stroke-width="2"/>
      <text x="215" y="117" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">Acquire Lock</text>

      <line x1="275" y1="112" x2="315" y2="112" stroke="#4a9e24" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrow4)"/>

      <rect x="315" y="85" width="110" height="55" rx="8" fill="#2b2b2b" stroke="#5DB92E" stroke-width="2"/>
      <text x="370" y="117" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700" fill="#5DB92E">Run Task</text>

    <div class="bx-faq">
    <h3 class="bx-h3">Frequently Asked Questions</h3>

    <div class="bx-faq-item">
      <button type="button" class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">1</span><span>Why do PHP cron jobs fail even when the script works fine manually?</span></button>
      <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>Cron provides almost none of a normal shell environment. Missing absolute paths and a minimal PATH are the most common causes of a script that works by hand but fails under cron.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="bx-faq-item">
      <button type="button" class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">2</span><span>How is an overlapping cron run actually prevented?</span></button>
      <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>A file lock acquired with flock() at the start of the script. If a second instance cannot acquire the lock, it exits immediately instead of running alongside the first.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="bx-faq-item">
      <button type="button" class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">3</span><span>Is redirecting output to a log file enough on its own?</span></button>
      <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>It helps, but a log nobody reads still allows a failure to go unnoticed. Pairing logging with an active alert on failure closes that gap.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="bx-faq-item">
      <button type="button" class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">4</span><span>When does a queue worker make more sense than a cron job?</span></button>
      <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>When work needs to happen the moment an event occurs rather than on a fixed schedule, or when built in retries and backpressure handling matter more than simplicity.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="bx-faq-item">
      <button type="button" class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">5</span><span>Should a scheduled task be tested by waiting for cron to trigger it?</span></button>
      <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>No. Running the exact crontab command by hand first catches most bugs immediately, rather than waiting for the schedule and hoping something logs the failure.</p></div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="bx-learn">
    <h2 id="what-we-learn-today">What We Learn Today</h2>
    <div class="bx-learn-grid">
      <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">1</span><div><h4>PHP cron jobs strip the shell environment</h4><p>Absolute paths avoid the most common cause of silent failure.</p></div></div>
      <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">2</span><div><h4>Overlap needs an explicit lock</h4><p>flock() stops a slow run from colliding with the next one.</p></div></div>
      <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">3</span><div><h4>Logging makes failure visible</h4><p>Nothing written down did not happen, as far as anyone can tell.</p></div></div>
      <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">4</span><div><h4>Alerts close the loop</h4><p>A log nobody reads still lets a failure run unnoticed.</p></div></div>
      <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">5</span><div><h4>Queue workers cover a different need</h4><p>Event driven work with retries fits queues better than a schedule.</p></div></div>
      <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">6</span><div><h4>Manual runs catch bugs faster</h4><p>Testing the exact crontab command beats waiting for the schedule.</p></div></div>
    </div>
  </div>

<script>
(function() {
  var items = document.querySelectorAll('.bx-faq-item');

  items.forEach(function(item) {
    var q = item.querySelector('.bx-faq-q');
    var a = item.querySelector('.bx-faq-a');

    item.classList.add('open');
    a.style.maxHeight = a.scrollHeight + 'px';

    q.addEventListener('click', function() {
      var isOpen = item.classList.contains('open');
      if (isOpen) {
        item.classList.remove('open');
        a.style.maxHeight = null;
      } else {
        item.classList.add('open');
        a.style.maxHeight = a.scrollHeight + 'px';
      }
    });
  });
})();
</script>
